headline: [[q|…Israel began committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.]] Two of the most-read opening sections now say it in Wikipedia’s own voice.
unit: sentences charging Israel with genocide: Jan 2021 · Jul 2023 · now, in the 150 most-read opening sections that existed in 2021 (plus Israel’s denial)
body: Own voice: the articles on Israel and on Benjamin Netanyahu; five others attribute the charge. No sentence in these 150 charges Hamas or Palestinians with genocide. (The October 7 article, outside this set, keeps one attributed: [[q|Some have alleged that the attack was an act of genocide or a genocidal massacre against Israelis.]])

headline: “Militant” left Hamas’s definition five days after October 7, replaced by “military”. The hostages are in neither the Hamas nor the Israel opening section.
unit: after October 7, “militant” became “military” in Hamas’s definition (12 Oct 2023); it came back three times, last in February 2025
body: Hamas is now [[q|a Sunni Islamist Palestinian nationalist political organisation with a military wing]]; the designation sentence moved from sentence 5 of 20 to 22 of 23.

headline: 1948 got an agent. The Nakba is now [[q|the ethnic cleansing of Palestinian Arabs by Zionists]], in Wikipedia’s own voice.
unit: the Nakba’s first sentence, in Wikipedia’s own voice, since 6 July 2026
body: Three of the four 1948 articles quoted in this report now name the agent (Nakba, 1948 Palestine war, 1948 Arab–Israeli War); the fourth, 1948 Palestinian expulsion and flight, removed it from its first sentence.

headline: Occupation is now stated as fact, for Israel as for Russia in Crimea and Turkey in Cyprus.
unit: of occupation charges against Israel stated in Wikipedia’s own voice (16 of 35 → 44 of 55)
body: Since the July 2024 ICJ advisory opinion, editors have a court to cite. Against Russia and Turkey: 2 of 8 to 14 of 19 (25% to 74%), on small counts. Many of the new Israel ones are history and events of 2024 to 2026.

headline: Canvassing is documented on both sides. The rewriting began in the war’s first weeks, before the Discord channel opened; ArbCom’s April 2025 finding of other coordination gives no start date.
unit: topic insertions of critical terms per week ÷ comparison, 16 weeks after 7 Oct 2023 (0.5× before the war; 2.0× while the Discord channel was active). Descriptive: a war on the topic’s own pages raises this by itself.
body: ArbCom found pro-Israel email canvassing (January 2024 motions) and sanctioned editors for acting on off-wiki canvassing from a pro-Palestinian Discord channel (December 2024).[[verify|ArbCom items read from search snippets only; check primary pages (ORGS.md section 5)]] Our footprint tests found no campaign signature and could only have seen very large effects.

headline: The pages readers reach first changed; the obscure ones changed no more than other conflicts’ pages.
unit: of Top-importance Israel, Palestine and Jewish-topic articles gained critical vocabulary in their opening paragraph since July 2023 (121 sampled); other conflict regions 4.4%; gap +5.9 points, range +0.9 to +11.2
body: Mid importance: 1.5% against none of the 362 comparison articles sampled; across all 49,000 articles the gap is 0.4 points, within the margin of error. Articles on Judaism did not move.
